1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Basmati is a famous and expensive rice. It grows in a place between India and Pakistan. This place is called Punjab.

Both countries want the name Basmati for themselves in the EU. A special name brings a lot of money and protection. India asks the EU for the name first, and Pakistan asks later. But the two countries do not talk to each other to solve the problem. Because there is no rule yet, many companies sell fake Basmati rice around the world. Almost 90% of Basmati rice in shops does not come from Punjab.

If Europe does not decide soon, the special name Basmati may not be important anymore.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Basmati is a very expensive type of rice from the Punjab region, but this region is divided between India and Pakistan.

Both countries want to protect the name Basmati in the EU to earn more money. If a name gets protection, other countries cannot use it. India asked the EU for special protection in 2018, and Pakistan asked in 2023. But the two countries don’t talk to each other, so they can’t make a shared decision.

Other places, like Cyprus with Halloumi cheese, worked together with the EU to protect their product. But because India and Pakistan are not talking, almost 90% of Basmati rice sold around the world is not real. If the EU doesn’t act soon, the name Basmati might lose its special value completely.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Basmati rice is one of the world’s most valuable rice varieties, and sells for up to twice the price of standard white rice. Both India and Pakistan grow this crop in the historical region of Punjab, which is now divided by an international border.

For years, both nations have been locked in a legal dispute over the exclusive right to the Basmati name in the EU. Receiving Protected Geographical Indication (PGI) status would grant a valuable market monopoly, but neither country has been able to submit a joint application due to a lack of political cooperation. Although similar disputes, such as Halloumi cheese in divided Cyprus, were resolved through joint EU frameworks, negotiations between India and Pakistan have completely stalled.

Without an agreement or EU protection, approximately 90% of rice sold globally under the name Basmati comes from other regions. Experts warn that if the EU delays its decision further it may destroy its protection completely.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Top leaders from Germany and Russia meet in New York. This is their first talk in over four years, since the start of the war in Ukraine.

The meeting is only 20 minutes long. Relations are bad. Germany says that Russia tries a drone attack on a German airport. The German leader asks Russia to stop dangerous actions in Europe. Russia says that the meeting does not change anything.

Germany still helps Ukraine, but both countries decided to talk face to face. World leaders hope that these small talks can slowly help bring peace in the future.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
German Foreign Minister met Russian Foreign Minister at the UN in New York. This was their first meeting since Russia invaded Ukraine over four years ago.

The talks lasted only 20 minutes and happened during a time of high tension between both countries. Germany recently accused Russia of planning a drone attack at a German airport. The German minister told Russia to stop its dangerous actions against Europe and NATO. Russia said the meeting changed nothing, and both countries disagreed on who asked for the talk.

Germany still strongly supports Ukraine with weapons and help. But this short meeting shows that leaders are starting to talk directly again as world organizations try to find peaceful solutions to end the war.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov held a brief 20-minute meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York.

This marked the first direct diplomatic encounter between top German and Russian officials since Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.

The meeting took place despite escalating tensions, following German accusations that Russia orchestrated a drone attack at Leipzig/Halle airport. During the talks, Wadephul urged Moscow to abandon its dangerous path of escalation toward Germany, Europe, and NATO. While Lavrov downplayed the event’s importance and claimed Germany made no position changes, diplomats noted the symbolic weight of reopening a direct channel. Both sides disputed who initiated the exchange.

Despite Germany’s primary role as a strategic supporter of Ukraine rather than a mediator, the meeting reflects broader shifts in diplomatic discussions as international leaders search for ways toward future negotiations.

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Many pregnant women die. Some have problems during pregnancy. Some die when they give birth.

In Africa, a pregnant woman dies every two minutes. It happens mainly in places like Kenya. Many people there live far from hospitals. They cannot get the right help. But now, there is a new device. It shows pictures of babies inside their moms. It is easy to use it. Even people who are not experts can do it. It can find problems early and save lives.

Experts are still testing the device. But many people believe that it can make a big difference for women in Kenya.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Every two minutes, a pregnant woman dies due to complications, mostly in places like Kenya.

Many people in sub-Saharan Africa live far from hospitals. They don’t get good care and it is difficult to get to hospitals. But new technology, like portable ultrasound devices, may help. Groups like Jakaranda Health and Google create devices which non-experts can use. The devices use AI to analyze scans and detect problems early, which can save lives.

Experts are still testing these devices which could greatly improve maternal healthcare in Kenya, where only a few mothers currently have access to ultrasounds.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Pregnancy-related complications claim a woman’s life every two minutes, with most deaths occurring in sub-Saharan Africa, notably Kenya.

Limited access to healthcare facilities, especially in remote rural areas where 70% of the population resides, exacerbates the issue. Challenges include inadequate healthcare workers and transportation barriers to reach hospitals. However, innovative solutions are emerging, such as mobile ultrasound technology pioneered by organizations like Jakaranda Health and Google. This portable system, coupled with artificial intelligence, enables non-sonographers to perform scans, potentially saving lives by detecting pregnancy complications early.

While still in trial phases, this advancement offers hope for improved maternal healthcare in Kenya, where only 10% of rural mothers currently have access to ultrasound services.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Scotland has a big crisis. Over 11,000 people die from drugs in ten years. Last year, 1,133 people die because strong new drugs come to the country.

The problem starts long ago when many people lose their jobs. They have no money. Political cuts to help centers also make things worse. Today, scientists test new drugs in a lab to keep people safe. Police work hard to stop dangerous drug sellers.

The government now gives more money for doctors, medicines, and help centers. These centers help people stop using drugs and start a happy, safe life again.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Scotland has a very big drug problem, with more than 11,000 drug deaths in ten years. Last year, 1,133 people died because new, dangerous synthetic drugs entered the market.

This crisis started years ago when factories closed, and many people lost work, hope, or support. Past government decisions to cut funding for help services also made the crisis worse. Now, Scotland is trying to fix this health emergency. Scientists are testing new drugs to help health workers respond quickly. Police are stopping drug sellers, and the government is funding overdose treatments, rehab centers, and safer places for users.

Recovery centers are helping people leave drugs behind. People who suffered from addiction can finally find a safe place to heal and start a new life.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Scotland faces a severe national crisis. It recorded over 11,000 drug-related deaths in the past decade, which made it the drug death capital of Europe.

In 2025 alone, 1,133 people died, driven by an increasingly dangerous supply of synthetic opioids like nitazenes.

The origins of this crisis trace back to 20th-century industrial decline, poverty, and intergenerational trauma. Additionally, political decisions worsened the situation, including controversial 2015 funding cuts to treatment services by the Scottish government, for which officials have since apologized. To combat the epidemic, Scotland is expanding its national drug testing facilities to identify rapid market changes and provide scientific evidence for public health policies.

Police continue seizing tens of millions of kilograms worth of illicit substances, while politicians advocate for harm-reduction measures, including safer consumption rooms and expanded rehabilitation spaces. Some facilities offer critical recovery programs, which give long-term users a safe environment to overcome addiction and rebuild their lives.

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Tokyo is the capital of Japan. Life in Tokyo is not cheap.

Young people do not have enough money. They have their first job. Sometimes they come from small towns. They cannot rent a big apartment. They live in so-called micro-apartments. A micro-apartment is a very small apartment. It has just nine square meters. It is very simple. There are not many things.

The monthly rent is between 380 and 610 dollars. The rent depends on where in Tokyo the apartment is. Young people prefer micro-apartments because they do not need to pay any deposit to the landlord.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
In the Japanese capital Tokyo, the so-called micro-apartments are a popular place for young people to live.

These apartments have just nine square meters and they are very simple. There are very few amenities and very little space to keep just everything you need. Monthly rent is 380 to 610 dollars, and it depends on where exactly in Tokyo the apartment is.

Micro-apartments are so popular with young people because they don’t have enough money for a bigger apartment. Many people come to live in Tokyo from other towns and they need a cheap place to stay. One benefit is that landlords don’t usually ask for any deposit.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Micro-apartments are places that are very small, have very few amenities, very little space, and not many of the home comforts that you’d associate with living in a bigger apartment and certainly in a house.

However, they’re becoming increasingly popular in the Japanese capital, particularly among younger people who’re just starting in the workplace and can’t afford rents for ordinary places, or they may be moving into Tokyo from out of town and want a cheap place to stay.

Each micro-apartment measures just nine square meters, which is under half the size of a typical studio apartment in Tokyo. The benefit’s that there’s zero deposit and no ‘key money’, a nonrefundable gift to the landlord. Monthly rents range from 380 to 610 dollars, depending on where in Tokyo you are.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
A woman uses Duolingo for 2,061 days. She loses her daily streak. She can see that she still can not speak Spanish.

Duolingo uses games, points, and notifications to make people use the app every day. The company also fires real teachers and uses AI computers to make quick lessons. But the lesson quality is bad. In 2026, the company loses a lot of money. People see that the app is not teaching real language skills.

Duolingo builds a game, but it does not help people speak to others.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
A Duolingo user lost a 2,061-day streak and realized she still couldn’t speak Spanish fluently. This showed a big problem with the popular language app.

Duolingo became very rich by using games, daily streaks, and notifications to keep people using the app every day. The company also replaced many human workers with cheap AI to build its courses, which made the lessons worse. Even though the company earned a lot of money, investors started to worry that users were not actually learning anything. The company’s stock price dropped by 80 percent by early 2026. Lawyers also started investigating the company for confusing investors about user growth.

In the end, Duolingo created a great game to keep people clicking, but it failed at its main job: teaching people how to talk to real speakers.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
A viral post by a user who lost a 2,061-day Duolingo streak exposed a fundamental flaw in the language-learning platform: years of daily app use failed to deliver actual conversational fluency.

Duolingo achieved massive financial success; it reached 1 billion dollars in revenue in 2025. How? By prioritizing gamification features like notifications, streak freezes, and leaderboards.

However, the company faced severe backlash after firing contractors to replace language courses with lower-quality generative AI content. This hyper-focus on user engagement over educational value eventually triggered a massive market correction. Duolingo’s stock plummeted roughly 80 percent from its peak near 544 dollars down to around 101 dollars by spring 2026. Investors grew skeptical as daily active user growth slowed, and law firms opened securities fraud investigations regarding potentially misleading growth metrics.

The dramatic financial collapse demonstrated that while Duolingo successfully optimized user habits, push notifications, and short-term corporate revenue, it failed to teach users how to speak new languages fluently.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
President Xi Jinping from China visits President Donald Trump in the US. They have a big meal together and say friendly words. But they do not solve many big problems.

The presidents have different ideas about money, AI, or Taiwan. They only agree to help trade for two short months. Another problem is with journalists. Some news companies can not show video of the visit. One photo of the presidents is edited. AI changes it.

The visit was good for talking, but the two big countries still have many problems to solve together. As a friendly gift, China will send two new giant pandas to a zoo in Atlanta.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping visited President Donald Trump in Washington. The two leaders had a big dinner and shared friendly words, but they didn’t solve their main problems. They only agreed to stop new trade tariffs for two months.

China wants the US to stop selling weapons to Taiwan, while the US wants better rules on AI and trade. There were also news problems because some TV reporters were not allowed inside the White House. People also noticed that an official photo of the leaders was edited. The biggest positive moment was when China promised to send two new giant pandas to a zoo in Atlanta. Experts say that even though the visit was friendly, it is still not clear if the two powerful countries can fix their biggest differences in the future.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has completed a high-profile state visit to Washington to meet with US President Donald Trump. Despite red carpets, lavish dinners, and warm words between the leaders, the summit brought little political success.

The two countries agreed to a brief two-month extension of a trade truce with lower tariffs; however, disputes remain regarding AI governance, trade, and Taiwan. Beijing stated that US military aid to Taiwan is an absolute red line. The visit was also marked by controversies: major news networks were temporarily banned from live White House coverage, and an official photograph of the leaders appeared to be edited using AI. However, China offered a gesture of goodwill by gifting two giant pandas to an Atlanta zoo.

Experts note that while the visit stabilized communications between the world’s two largest superpowers, the true test of the relationship will depend on whether key trade and security issues are successfully resolved early next year.

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Rick Wakeman is a famous musician. He plays the piano for 150 bears at a big park in Vietnam. People save them from bad farms.

On these farms, farmers keep bears in small cages. They use the bears for medicine. Wakeman plays soft music on a big piano to make the animals happy. He wants to help 125 more bears. These bears are still in small cages. Many of these sick bears die every month.

Wakeman speaks to the government. He wants to save the animals fast so they can play on the green grass at the sanctuary.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Musician Rick Wakeman played a piano concert for 150 rescued bears in Vietnam. The performance took place outside at a large animal sanctuary in Tam Dao National Park.

Wakeman wrote special gentle music to make the bears feel happy and calm. He wanted to help 125 other bears that are still kept in small metal cages on bile farms. People on these farms keep bears in tiny spaces and take liquid from their gallbladders for traditional medicine.

Wakeman started supporting the sanctuary in 2016 and even adopted a young bear. He hopes his music concert will help people understand the problem and convince the government to move the rest of the bears from the farms to the safe sanctuary soon, where they can run, play, and live on green grass.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Former Yes musician Rick Wakeman performed a live piano concert for 150 rescued moon bears at the Animals Asia sanctuary in Vietnam’s Tam Dao National Park.

Wakeman played gentle, melodic original compositions on a grand piano set up near the enclosure perimeter to bring attention to the plight of Asiatic black bears in East Asia. The performance sought to highlight the remaining 125 bears still trapped in small cages on illegal bear bile farms, where about four animals die each month. In these facilities, bile is painfully extracted from the animals’ gallbladders for traditional medicine.

Wakeman, a long-time supporter of animal welfare who has sponsored rescue bears since 2016, expressed deep concern over the cruel conditions the animals endure. He urged the Vietnamese government to quickly release the remaining captive bears so they can experience open space and proper care at the sanctuary before it is too late.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Many people in London do not want to buy flats today. In the past, people wait in lines to buy them, but now many flats stay empty for months.

Buying a flat is very expensive. It is expensive to build a flat. Also, banks want a lot more money. Many owners are sad. They cannot sell their homes. Some flats have broken gas pipes or dangerous walls from old fires. Owners do not fix the problems quickly.

Because of these problems, many young people cannot move to bigger homes. The government is trying to make buying homes cheaper and safer for everyone.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
The flat market in London is facing big problems. A few years ago, many people waited in long lines to buy apartments. Today, half of the flats for sale cannot find a buyer.

This happens because buying a home is now very expensive due to high interest rates, rising maintenance costs, and a growing need for bigger houses. Many apartment owners feel trapped in bad situations. In one building, residents had no hot water for months, but they couldn’t sell their flats because the building managers argued about who should pay for repairs. In addition, thousands of flats still have dangerous walls after the Grenfell fire tragedy, which makes them impossible to sell.

The government is trying to fix these issues by lowering required cash deposits and ending unfair lease rules.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
London’s real estate market is facing a severe slump in flat sales, which is in sharp contrast with the high demand seen just a few years ago.

Property data reveals a growing mismatch in the housing crisis: 88 percent of flats listed for sale in London last year failed to find a buyer within six months.

High mortgage rates, rising service charges, and changing post-pandemic preferences for larger living spaces have combined to make flats far less attractive compared to houses. Complex leasehold structures, ongoing maintenance issues, and unresolved building defects further paralyze the market. Residents in Croydon are left without hot water or heating due to gas leaks, yet they cannot sell their properties because management companies clash over repair bills. Meanwhile, unresolved fire safety regulations following the Grenfell tragedy leave thousands of buildings with unsafe cladding, which prevents owners from selling.

The UK government is introducing measures to cap ground rents and speed up cladding removal to help restore stability.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
An important politician in Malaysia, Anthony Loke, wants to quit his job as transport minister. He is unhappy because ex leader Najib Razak can leave prison to live at home under house arrest.

Anthony Loke says that all people must follow the law. His political party is very big and strong. Other ministers in his party will stay in the government. They want to keep the country safe and stable so the government does not end.

Loke says that public buses and train projects will keep working normally.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Malaysia’s Transport Minister offered to quit his government job. He is angry because the country’s king gave a special pardon to former Prime Minister Najib Razak.

Under this new rule, Najib can leave prison and stay under house arrest if he pays a large fine. Loke said his party is strongly against corruption and believes that no one is above the law. But to keep the country’s government stable, only Anthony Loke offered to step down. Other ministers from his party will stay in their posts so the Prime Minister’s government doesn’t fall.

Loke promised that big national transport projects will continue as planned without any problems.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Malaysia’s Transport Minister Anthony Loke offered to resign from the cabinet in protest against a conditional royal pardon granted to jailed former Prime Minister Najib Razak.

The pardon allows Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest if he meets specific conditions, including paying a fine of approximately 12 million dollars. Loke, who serves as the Secretary-General of the Democratic Action Party (DAP), emphasized that keeping Najib behind bars is a firm boundary for the party due to its long-standing fight against corruption and commitment to justice.

Despite Loke’s personal resignation offer, the DAP central executive committee decided that its four other ministers and seven deputy ministers will remain in government. DAP is the largest party in the ruling coalition. It holds 40 parliamentary seats and aims to protect political stability and prevent the collapse of the Prime Minister’s unity government. Loke assured the public that key national transport projects will continue without disruption.

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
The doorway effect is a common problem with your memory. You walk into a room and forget why you are there.

This happens because your brain thinks that a new event is starting when you walk through a door. To get ready for new things, your brain clears your memory. Scientists test this in real and virtual rooms. People forget more when they go through doors or do many things at once. Changing computer tabs can do the same thing.

If you forget your goal, you can walk back to the first room or say your idea again out loud.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
The doorway effect happens when you walk into a new room and suddenly forget what you were going to do.

Scientists explain that our brains divide our daily life into different events. When you go through a door, your brain thinks a new event is starting. It clears your short-term memory to make space for new information, which can make you forget your previous thought. Studies show that passing through doorways makes people forget things more easily, especially when they are multitasking or moving through many rooms. Similar things happen when you change tabs on a computer or get distracted.

To remember what you forgot, you can walk back to the previous room or repeat your goal out loud while moving.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
The doorway effect, also known as the location updating effect, is a common memory lapse that occurs when walking into a new room makes you forget your original intention.

Psychologists explain that our brains break continuous time into separate events.

When moving through a doorway or entering a new space, the brain identifies an event boundary. It saves the previous event model into long-term memory and clears short-term memory to prepare for incoming information, and sometimes accidentally erases thoughts you still need. Scientific experiments using physical and virtual environments show that passing through doorways slows response times and increases forgetting, especially when people are multitasking. Similar memory lapses can be triggered by changing computer tabs, time jumps in stories, or sudden distractions. However, event boundaries can also help organize information by preventing interference between tasks. To recover lost thoughts, scientists suggest retracing your physical steps or consciously repeating your goal as you move between spaces.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
A big study says that Greenland and Antarctica lose a lot of ice since 1979. Warm water and warm air are melting the ice very fast.

This lost ice makes the sea level 3.2 centimetres higher around the world. When the sea goes up, it brings big floods. It is dangerous for people who live near the ocean. Every centimetre of sea level rise can flood millions of homes.

Scientists look at satellite pictures for forty years. They say that the ice is safe in the past. But now it melts faster and faster every year. The water will keep going up if the planet stays warm.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
A new study shows that Greenland and Antarctica lost 12.5 trillion tonnes of ice since 1979. This huge melting of ice caused world sea levels to rise by about 3.2 centimetres.

Scientists used satellite data to track the changes over forty years. They discovered that the ice sheets were stable in the 1970s and 1980s, but melting became much faster after 1990. Warmer ocean water causes most of this damage by melting ice from under the glaciers. Scientists explain that every centimetre of higher sea level puts two to three million more people at risk of dangerous flooding.

Even though ice loss slowed down a little bit between 2020 and 2023, experts warn that this was only short-term weather and the long-term trend remains very dangerous.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
A major scientific study reveals that Greenland and Antarctica have lost 12.5 trillion tonnes of ice since 1979.

This massive loss has raised global sea levels by approximately 3.2 centimetres. Based on more than four decades of satellite observations, researchers found that while the ice sheets remained relatively stable through the 1970s and 1980s, melting accelerated significantly in the 1990s and reached its fastest rate during the 2010s. Rising air and ocean temperatures drive this destruction, with warmer seawater responsible for about 84 percent of the ice loss by melting glaciers from below.

In Greenland, the Jakobshavn glacier is now retreating by up to 50 metres per day. Experts warn that for every centimetre of sea level rise, two to three million additional people face annual coastal flooding. Although ice loss temporarily slowed between 2020 and 2023 due to short-term weather patterns, scientists emphasize that the long-term melting trend continues.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
In China, many people use a phone app. The app helps them feel safe.

The app asks one question each day. The question is: “Are you dead?” People tap the phone to say that they are okay. If they do not tap for two days, the app sends a message to family or friends.

Many people in China live alone now. Fewer people marry. Older people often live without their children. Sometimes, people from work know more about a person than their family. Older people worry about getting help.

People talk less face-to-face. But phones are not the same as real people. People are online all the time, but they feel lonely. You need to be with others to feel good and healthy.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
In China, many people now pay for a phone app that asks one clear question each day: “Are you dead?”

The app is for people who live alone and worry that no one will notice if something bad happens to them. Users tap once a day to show they are safe. If they don’t tap for two days, the app sends a message to chosen people.

Since it started last year, the app became very popular. The app shows a big social change. More people in China live alone because fewer people marry, and many older people live without family. Often, workmates notice problems before family or friends do. Experts say people feel more alone today, even though they use phones and online tools all the time.

Studies show loneliness affects both older people and young people. Online contact is not the same as contact with another person. Time with other people in real life still matters because it makes people feel connected and well.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
In China, millions of people now pay for an app that asks them one simple question each day: “Are you dead?”

The app targets people who live alone and worry that no one will notice if something bad happens to them. Users tap once a day to show they are safe. If they don’t respond for two days, the app sends a message to chosen contacts.

Since it started last year, the app has become one of the most popular paid apps in the country. The app shows a big social change. More people in China live alone because fewer people marry, and many older adults live without family. Often, work contacts notice problems sooner than relatives. Experts say people feel more alone today, even though digital communication is everywhere.

Studies show loneliness affects people of all ages. Online contact cannot fully replace a real human connection. Time with other people in real life still matters most for feeling connected and well.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Liberland is a plan for a new country on a small piece of land in Europe. A Czech man named Vít Jedlička starts it in 2015.

The man wants a place with no taxes and no big government rules. Some people buy passports. They want more freedom. But Liberland is not a real country today. No other country says that it is real. Police from Croatia watch the border and stop people from living there. There are no houses or towns, only trees and a beach next to the river.

Many people like the dream of Liberland, but they cannot move there yet.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Liberland is a new project to start a country on a small piece of land near the Danube River between Serbia and Croatia. It was created in 2015 by a man from the Czech Republic named Vít Jedlička.

He wants to build a state with no taxes and very few laws. People who give more money will have more power in the government.

Many people like this idea because they want more freedom from traditional governments. But the project has many big problems. No official country recognizes Liberland, and Croatian police stop people from living there permanently.

At this moment, Liberland has no real roads or houses, only two tree houses and a small beach. While supporters hope for a better future, Liberland remains just a big dream rather than a real country.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Liberland is a self-proclaimed libertarian micro-state located on a small piece of land along the Danube between Croatia and Serbia.

Founded in 2015 by Czech politician Vít Jedlička, the project takes advantage of an unresolved border dispute following the breakup of Yugoslavia. Jedlička aims to create a tax-free, digital state based on meritocracy, where financial contributions grant citizens greater political power than traditional democracy allows. This idea attracts global supporters who feel restricted by taxes and government control; however,

Liberland faces severe practical and legal obstacles. Croatian authorities strictly guard the area, prohibit permanent settlement, and destroy unauthorized infrastructure. Furthermore, no sovereign country recognizes Liberland as an independent state. Visitors and prospective citizens, such as Italian project manager Antonella, view the project as an inspiring alternative to modern governments. However, critics describe it as a utopian experiment that exists as little more than a makeshift campsite on the riverbank.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Snowflakes form when water meets tiny objects in clouds.

Snowflakes have different shapes. Their shape depends on temperature and on how much water is in the air. Snowflakes seem white. But they are clear. The light makes them look white. They have symmetry, too. It means that all parts look similar. They are pleasant to look at.

In 1611, Johannes Kepler wonders why snowflakes have six sides. He believes that this is because of good use of space. Scientists prove this hundreds of years later.

You can photograph snowflakes. But you need to be patient. It is not easy. It takes a lot of time to take a perfect picture of a snowflake.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Snowflakes form when water vapor meets dust or pollen in the clouds. They all have different shapes due to different temperature and humidity.

In 1611, Johannes Kepler wondered why snowflakes had six sides. He thought that it was an efficient use of space. Scientists proved this theory centuries later. Although snowflakes appear white, they are clear. Their symmetry is pleasing to the human brain, much like other symmetrical objects in nature. Snowflakes fall thanks to gravity and they follow universal laws of physics, just like objects in space.

Photographing snowflakes requires perfect conditions and a lot of patience.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Snowflakes, with their intricate and captivating beauty, can be explained by the universal laws of nature.

A snowflake, technically called a snow crystal, forms when water vapor meets tiny specks of dust or pollen in the clouds. This interaction creates a hexagonal structure with branching tips that attract more water molecules, resulting in the unique shape of each snowflake. Temperature and humidity determine the size and shape of these branches as the snowflake falls through the clouds due to gravity. No two snowflakes are alike due to their individual journeys.

In 1611, Johannes Kepler theorized about the hexagonal pattern of snowflakes, which was later proven as an efficient use of space. Despite their white appearance, snowflakes are actually clear, with light scattering from their edges. Snowflakes, like celestial bodies, demonstrate the laws of physics and carry their unique history, much like humans.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Singer Ed Sheeran has a big problem on his tour in the US. His guest singer, Macklemore, speaks about Palestine on stage. The stadium owner gets angry. He asks Sheeran to drop Macklemore from the show.

Sheeran does it. He wants to keep his tour going. After this, all the other guest singers quit the tour. They think that artists must speak freely on stage. At his next big show in Philadelphia, Sheeran plays alone, only with his guitar.

Sheeran says sorry to his fans for making mistakes. He calls the war in Gaza terrible. He will finish all his concerts alone.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Musician Ed Sheeran is facing serious problems on his American tour after all of his opening artists quit. The trouble started when rapper Macklemore showed pictures of war and called for a free Palestine during a concert.

The billionaire owner of the stadium told Sheeran to remove Macklemore or cancel his shows. Sheeran let Macklemore leave because he wanted to save jobs for his crew members, but other musicians were angry about this decision. They left the tour because they believe artists should speak freely.

At his first solo concert in Philadelphia, Sheeran spoke directly to the crowd. He apologized for his mistakes and called the situation in Gaza catastrophic and wrong. Sheeran will now play all the remaining big concerts completely alone with just his guitar.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
British pop star Ed Sheeran faces a major crisis on his US tour after his supporting acts all withdrew following a high-profile controversy.

The conflict began when rapper Macklemore made pro-Palestinian statements and displayed images of war during a performance at Gillette Stadium in New Jersey.

In response, the stadium owner and other venue managers presented Sheeran with an ultimatum: remove Macklemore or cancel the concerts. Sheeran accepted Macklemore’s removal to protect his tour crew’s livelihoods, but this decision sparked outrage among fellow artists, who all quit in protest against censorship by venue owners.

At his opening solo concert in Philadelphia, Sheeran addressed the controversy directly on stage without any supporting acts. He apologized for his handling of the situation and voiced deep concern over stadium owners dictating artistic content. He condemned the October 7 attacks as horrific and described the ongoing devastation in Gaza as catastrophic. Sheeran will complete the remaining stadium dates alone.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Reading test scores for teenagers are falling in many countries. Experts say that screens make young people read too fast. Children skim words on their phones and tablets. They do not understand the main ideas.

Also, using AI to write paper assignments stops the brain from learning. This is bad for the future. People need to read to think well. If not, they easily believe fake news and bad information.

But we can change this situation. Parents should read books to young children every day. Reading real books for 20 minutes a day helps the brain grow strong and keeps reading skills safe.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Tests show that teenage reading skills are dropping rapidly around the world. Experts say reading on digital screens turns young people into hasty readers.

Instead of reading carefully, students skim texts. This means they don’t fully understand what they read.

Using AI tools to write assignments also stops students from practicing deep reading and writing. This trend is dangerous for society and democracy. If young people cannot understand complex information, they cannot make good decisions as informed voters.

But we can fix this problem. Countries like Estonia use technology to make students think harder, not to make work too easy. Parents can help by reading to young children and encouraging everyone to read physical books for 20 minutes every day.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
International test results reveal a sharp decline in teenage reading skills across 91 countries since 2012. Experts argue that digital screens are transforming young readers into hasty readers or skimmers.

Because students read quickly on digital devices without allocating time and effort to complex comprehension, they fail to develop critical thinking skills. Furthermore, rising reliance on AI text generators like ChatGPT lets students skip essential writing processes, which further weakens the neural circuits required for deep reading and critical analysis.

This decline poses significant risks to democratic societies. Without strong reading skills, future voters become far more vulnerable to misinformation, demagoguery, and algorithmic control. However, experts emphasize that this trend can be changed. Countries like Estonia and Singapore successfully integrate technology in schools to support cognitive skills rather than passive consumption. Reversing the decline requires starting early by reading to children and establishing daily habits of reading challenging printed books.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Jared Kushner is Donald Trump’s son-in-law. He works as a very important diplomat for the United States. But he also has his own business.

Some people worry about his foreign money and business. But he still has an important job in the government. Kushner talks to leaders in other countries to help stop wars in places like Ukraine. Many leaders like to talk to him because he is part of the president’s family.

But some people say that mixing family, money, and government work can cause problems. Kushner stays very close to the president, so his power is very strong today.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of Donald Trump, is one of the most powerful diplomats in the United States. He grew up in a wealthy real estate family and later joined Trump’s team as a close adviser.

Although security officials worried about his foreign business connections, he was given special access to high-level diplomatic talks in places like Ukraine and the Middle East. Many critics worry about conflicts of interest because Kushner created a business that received billions of dollars from Saudi Arabia. But foreign leaders often work with him because they know he speaks directly to the president.

Experts say having a family member act as a private businessman and international diplomat creates a new and unusual situation in modern American history.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Jared Kushner, Donald Trump’s son-in-law, serves as a high-level diplomatic envoy despite having no prior background in public service.

Kushner grew up in a prominent New Jersey real estate family and became a trusted adviser during Trump’s initial political campaign.

Although foreign business ties raised security concerns and blocked his clearance, those issues were ultimately dismissed, and he was granted access to international negotiations in regions like Gaza and Ukraine. Kushner’s dual role as a private businessman and diplomat has raised serious conflict-of-interest questions. After leaving government, his private equity firm secured massive investments from Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund.

While diplomats recognize his ability to communicate directly with the president, experts caution that negotiating through Kushner remains unpredictable given Trump’s changing decisions. Despite potential security and financial concerns, Kushner’s position within the president’s family ensures his continued global influence.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
The European Central Bank shows ten designs for new euro money. Bank leaders choose from 1,200 ideas. They pick two main topics.

The first topic shows famous people like Leonardo da Vinci, Marie Curie, and Beethoven. The second topic shows birds and rivers to help protect nature. Now, people who live in Europe can choose their favorite design. They can vote on the bank’s website.

After the vote, the bank will make the new paper money. People will start to use the new euro money at the end of 2026.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
The European Central Bank has shown ten finalist designs for new euro cash notes. Over 1,200 ideas were sent in, but leaders chose two big ideas to show European culture and nature.

The first idea features famous historic leaders in art, science, and music, such as Leonardo da Vinci, Maria Callas, Marie Curie, and Beethoven. The second idea features wild birds and beautiful rivers, and shows the need to protect nature and animals across Europe.

People living in the EU can vote for their favorite idea in an online survey on the bank’s website. After the vote, the central bank will start printing the new paper money. People are expected to start using these new euro notes from the end of 2026.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde has unveiled ten shortlisted design concepts for future euro banknotes, selected from over 1,200 proposals.

The designs represent two main themes chosen to reflect European identity. The first theme focuses on prominent cultural figures in history, including artist Leonardo da Vinci, opera singer Maria Callas, scientist Marie Curie, and composer Ludwig van Beethoven. The second theme highlights nature and depicts various European bird species in river landscapes alongside major European Union institutions to emphasize Europe’s biodiversity and environmental protection.

For the first time, European citizens will participate in selecting the final theme through an online survey hosted on the central bank’s website. Following the public vote and final design selection, technical preparation and production stages will begin. The new banknotes, which will be worth from 5 to 500 euros, are expected to enter circulation starting from the end of 2026.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
The war in Yemen is getting very bad. Houthi fighters are attacking government soldiers in the desert. Videos show burning trucks, big guns, and explosions.

Houthi forces say that they are winning the fight. The Saudi-backed government is using planes to attack Houthi soldiers from the sky. Because of the dangerous fighting, many families must run away from their homes. People walk at night with no food, no water, and no money.

Now, many mothers, fathers, and children live in small tents in camps. They need help because the war is starting in new places.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Fighting in Yemen is getting worse as Houthi forces attack Saudi-backed government troops in the Al Jawf area. Houthi media showed videos of destroyed military trucks, rockets, and heavy fighting in the desert.

The Houthis say they killed many enemy soldiers and destroyed their weapons during several days of conflict. At the same time, the Saudi-backed government released air force pictures showing strikes against Houthi fighters and equipment to stop their advance.

Because of the heavy fighting and air attacks, many families escaped their homes. People walked at night without food or water while bullets flew around them. Many displaced families now live in simple tents in camps near Aden, and hope the dangerous conflict will stop soon.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
The long-standing conflict in Yemen is intensifying as Houthi forces launch a major offensive against Saudi-backed government troops in the eastern province of Al Jawf.

Media released by the Houthi group shows extensive battlefield footage, including destroyed armored vehicles, heavy machine-gun fire from pickup trucks, and intense ground fighting across desert trenches.

Houthi forces claim to have inflicted heavy losses on government troops as their offensive gains momentum. In response, the Saudi-backed coalition has released aerial footage depicting retaliatory airstrikes aimed at stopping the Houthi advance and destroying military equipment.

As the violence spreads, innocent civilians bear the burden of the expanding war. Families are fleeing active battle zones on foot under heavy gunfire, and they often travel for days without food or water. Many displaced residents now arrive at makeshift camps outside Aden while the broader conflict continues to escalate.

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
US President Donald Trump says that fears about AI are not real. He wants the US to win the AI race. It will make the country strong.

Some tech leaders say that people should trust them to make AI safe. They do not want new laws. But many politicians want strong safety rules. Some politicians say that AI can be very dangerous, even more than nuclear bombs.

Some people believe that big companies only want to make money. Normal people will take all the risks. Experts say that we need good rules today to keep everyone safe in the future.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
US President Donald Trump called AI safety fears a hoax and said the country must win the global AI race. He believes AI will bring economic growth bigger than oil or diamonds.

But many people and experts disagree on how to manage this new technology. OpenAI leader Sam Altman says people should trust tech companies, while Nvidia’s CEO believes businesses should control their own safety rules without new government laws. Some politicians warned that AI could be more dangerous than nuclear weapons.

Many critics worry that big companies want all the profits, but at the same time, ordinary people will be at risk. Experts argue that the US needs strict rules to protect people and set a good example for the rest of the world.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Tech executives are divided on AI regulation. OpenAI boss Sam Altman acknowledged public fears while urging trust in developers. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang opposed new laws and stated that companies should self-regulate product safety.

Sanders warned that AI risks could exceed those of nuclear weapons, and urged lawmakers to prevent corporations from socializing the risks while keeping the financial profits. Politicians across the political spectrum are demanding strict restrictions; however, US President Donald Trump has dismissed safety fears surrounding AI as a hoax. He argued against slowing down development because the country that leads in AI wins globally. Trump highlighted the technology’s immense economic potential and compared its value to big industries like oil and diamonds.

Experts emphasize that the United States must establish strong domestic oversight to set international standards. Tech companies often leverage the idea of a global race with China to justify moving forward without adequate laws.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Joanna Wietrzyk is an athlete from Australia. She wins a big fitness race in Beijing, China. But she was very sick during the event.

Joanna has bad stomach problems. She has feces on her legs. She makes the sports equipment dirty. After the race, she goes to a hospital. She puts a photo on the internet. She is happy to win the race. Some people say that she is very strong. Other people say that it is dirty and dangerous for other runners.

Nobody stops Joanna during the race. People on the internet ask why. The workers at the event must clean the room. They put down new carpets. Many people now talk about how safe sport is for athletes.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Australian fitness athlete Joanna Wietrzyk won a big indoor competition in Beijing, China. But her victory caused a lot of discussion because she was very sick during the race.

Wietrzyk had severe stomach problems and left feces on shared sports equipment and carpets. After winning, she went to the hospital and posted a picture on social media. In the post, she wrote A win is a win. Some people praised her because she worked very hard and didn’t stop although she had problems. But many other people were angry. They said her condition was unsafe and dirty for other athletes.

People also asked why the organizers didn’t stop her to give her medical care. The event organizers had to close some lanes, change the carpet, and clean everything carefully. The story shows a big debate about sports rules and athlete health.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Australian athlete Joanna Wietrzyk won her age category at a Hyrox indoor fitness competition in Beijing, but her victory created significant controversy.

While competing, she suffered severe bowel incontinence and left feces on shared equipment such as rowers and carpeted areas.

Wietrzyk finished the race in just over an hour and later shared a photo from a hospital bed on an IV drip with the caption A win is a win. Opinions on the incident are deeply divided. Some fans praised her determination, mental strength, and refusal to give up under extreme physical distress. However, critics, commentators, and fellow participants highlighted the serious biological hazard her condition presented to other competitors. Many questioned why organizers didn’t intervene and stop her to provide medical help, especially since existing rules already penalized spitting and littering. Organizers had to close affected lanes, replace carpet, and deep clean the venue overnight, while debate continues over athlete health and safety protocols.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Scientists find the brightest object in the universe. It is as bright as 500 trillion suns.

Scientists use a big telescope in Chile to find the object. They call it J0529-4351. There is a black hole inside. It is the fastest-growing black hole ever. At first, scientists think that it is a nearby star. The object is 12 billion light-years away from us. This makes it even more amazing. It is a special kind of object called a quasar. Quasars are very bright and they produce a lot of energy.

This discovery makes scientists wonder how big black holes form so early in the universe. There are many questions now.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Scientists discovered the brightest object in the universe, and they named it J0529-4351. They used the Very Large Telescope in Chile.

The object is a quasar, a very big object which emits large amounts of energy. It shines 500 trillion times brighter than the Sun and hosts the fastest-growing black hole scientists ever recorded. The distance from Earth is 12 billion light-years, and it emphasizes the object’s brightness.

These findings challenge all we know about the early universe and how it formed. It suggests that black holes formed shortly after the Big Bang. Understanding this could help scientists find out what happened in the early days of the universe.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Astronomers have identified the most luminous object ever observed in the far reaches of space, named J0529-4351.

Detected by the Very Large Telescope in Chile, this object is a quasar, shining 500 trillion times brighter than the Sun. It hosts the fastest-growing black hole ever recorded, consuming mass equal to one Sun daily. Initially mistaken for a nearby star, J0529-4351’s true distance of 12 billion light-years emphasizes its intrinsic brightness.

Quasars like this one, with supermassive black holes at their cores, challenge existing theories about the early universe’s formation. The discovery underscores the mystery of how such massive black holes formed so early in cosmic history. Scientists speculate that these findings may provide insights into the fundamental nature of black hole formation shortly after the Big Bang.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Today, many children do not play with normal toys. Instead, they want iPhones, adult makeup, and body sprays.

Small children watch social media videos on phones and iPads. They see adults who use beauty products. Children want to do the same. But using adult skincare can hurt a child’s skin. Big stores and companies make a lot of money from young buyers.

Many young kids do not want to go to school. They want to become famous online. Parents spend a lot of money on these things for their children. Experts say that kids need less screen time, fewer products, and more time to play outside like in the past.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Today, adults buy more toys than children do, while young kids want adult items like smartphones, makeup, and expensive perfume.

Thanks to social media apps like TikTok, young boys and girls are watching videos about beauty and grooming routines. Many eight-year-old children are using adult skincare products, which can hurt their skin. Big companies are happy about this trend because they make a lot of money selling products to young buyers. In addition, many children now say they want to be famous online influencers instead of going to school or playing outside.

Although big tech companies and advertisers encourage this consumer behavior, parents are the ones buying these products. Experts say parents should limit screen time and help their children enjoy a real, simple childhood.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
A major generational shift is transforming childhood into an era of intense consumerism.

Today, more toys are sold to adults than to children, while kids, often referred to as Generation Alpha, are opting for iPhones, adult skincare, and expensive colognes instead.

Driven by viral TikTok trends like looksmaxxing and beauty tutorials, eight-year-olds are doing complex multi-step grooming routines. This shift has led to instances where young children apply harsh acids and retinols meant for older skin, which is causing physical damage. Corporations and beauty brands aggressively capitalize on this trend. They view young children as lifelong customers and adjust marketing strategies specifically toward them.

Meanwhile, over 60 percent of surveyed students express a desire to become influencers, and they frequently neglect formal education and creative play. While social media platforms and corporate marketing build this consumer pipeline, millennial parents finance these purchases. Critics argue that parents must intervene to restore traditional, screen-free childhood experiences.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Josef Průša is a Czech inventor. He changes the world of 3D printing.

As a student, he likes working with music equipment. He needs special parts for his projects. So, he decides to build his own 3D printer. His design becomes very popular. In 2012, he starts a company called Prusa Research in Prague. Today, the company sells printers all over the world and works with big organizations like NASA and Mercedes. Many small businesses also use his printers to make creative products.

Josef Průša believes that 3D printing can help more people create and build new things in Europe and beyond.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Josef Průša is a Czech entrepreneur and engineer who became one of Europe’s most influential people in 3D printing. As a student, he experimented with music technology and built his first 3D printer to make customized parts.

His design quickly gained global interest, and in 2012, he founded Prusa Research in Prague. The company now employs over 1,000 people and sells 3D printers to customers on every continent, including large organizations such as NASA, Mercedes, and MIT.

Průša’s open-source approach inspires countless small companies to innovate using cheaper printers locally. He believes 3D printing can bring manufacturing back to Europe by helping entrepreneurs design, produce, and compete independently.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Czech visionary Josef Průša has redefined additive manufacturing through his pioneering 3D printing technology.

Originally a student fascinated by music equipment, he engineered his own self-replicating 3D printer, an innovation that soon became an industry standard.

In 2012, he left university to establish Prusa Research, which has since evolved into a global enterprise based in Prague. The firm employs more than 1,200 people, exports worldwide, and generates annual revenues exceeding 160 million euros. Its award-winning machines are used by leading institutions such as NASA, CERN, and MIT, as well as numerous startups.

Průša’s philosophy centers on decentralizing production and stimulating European innovation. By making high-quality 3D printing accessible, he envisions a future where creativity, technology, and sustainability merge to reshape manufacturing across the continent.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
England will let local leaders add a small tax to overnight hotel stays. People who stay in hotels, B&Bs, or holiday homes will pay a little extra money, usually under 5% of the room cost.

Some cities like Manchester already have a tax of 1 pound (1.14 euros) per room. The new plan will start before 2029. Many hotel owners do not like this new tax. They worry that visitors will go to other places to save money.

Studies show that a 10-pound (11.40 euros) fee might make people visit less. But each local leader can choose to use the tax or say no to it.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
England will soon allow local mayors to charge a tourist tax on overnight hotel stays.

The tax will cover all types of places to stay, like hotels, B&Bs, and holiday homes. Mayors can choose the exact price, but most plan to keep it under 5% of the total room bill.

Cities like Manchester, which charges 1 pound (1.14 euros) per room, and Edinburgh already use similar fees. The new tax will likely start before 2029. Many businesses in the tourism industry are unhappy about the new tax. They worry that visitors will choose other places to travel to avoid paying extra fees, which could lead to a 1.8 billion pound (2.1 billion euros) loss in tourism spending. Studies show that many tourists might stay fewer nights or spend less money.

Mayors don’t have to introduce the tax, and some local leaders already said no to the plan.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
The UK government will allow mayors in England to introduce a tourist tax on overnight stays before 2029. The levy will apply to all accommodation types, including hotels, B&Bs, and short-term rentals, regardless of the visitor’s nationality or purpose.

While the charge is uncapped, local leaders, including London’s mayor, expect to keep it under 5% of the total accommodation cost. Similar fees are already operational in Manchester and Edinburgh, following widespread adoption across continental Europe. However, the hospitality sector has strongly criticized the decision. Experts warn that a 5% tax could reduce tourism spending by 1.8 billion pounds (2.1 billion euros) and destroy nearly 33,000 jobs by 2030. Furthermore, extra fees might deter both international and domestic travelers and drive them toward destinations without visitor levies.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Gamescom is the world’s biggest event for video games. More than 350,000 people visit to play new games.

This time, the event shows big news, like a new remake of The Witcher 3. Xbox celebrates 25 years and wants to make games cheaper for everyone. Famous characters like Lara Croft from Tomb Raider are coming back with new graphics. Small teams of workers are also making big games today. The company Nvidia shows new AI tools. They make games look like real life. Gamescom is a fun place for people to meet and play together.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Gamescom is the world’s biggest gaming event, with over 350,000 visitors. The event started with big news, including a new version of The Witcher 3.

At the show, Xbox celebrated its 25th birthday, and its new leader said the gaming industry needs to make hardware more affordable. Classic games are also coming back; Tomb Raider is getting a modern update called Legacy of Atlantis with better graphics and controls. Smaller game studios are working on big projects too. A small team from Scotland is making a new horror game called Silent Hill Townfall. Furthermore, technology companies like Nvidia showed new AI tools to make game graphics look very real in real time.

Gamescom remains an exciting place where fans and developers meet to play new games.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Gamescom, the world’s largest in-person gaming convention, opened with Opening Night Live and featured major announcements like a remake of The Witcher 3.

Over 350,000 visitors are expected at the massive event that fills ten halls with major publishers and indie developers.

CEO Asha Sharma marked Xbox’s 25th anniversary and emphasized that the industry must innovate on efficiency and hardware affordability. Classic franchises are also making headlines; Tomb Raider is being reimagined as Legacy of Atlantis with modernized gameplay while it honors Lara Croft’s iconic confidence.

Smaller independent studios are stepping up to handle huge intellectual properties. Scottish team Screenburn is developing Silent Hill Townfall. Tech advancements are equally prominent – Nvidia demonstrates DLSS 5, a generative AI graphics tool that renders hyper-realistic visuals in real time. Gamescom highlights how the industry is adapting to new challenges, balancing iconic remakes with groundbreaking technology to shape gaming’s future.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
In Gambia, many people do not have electricity. Some places have no power for two days in the hot weather.

People are very angry because their food spoils. Shops cannot work. Protesters walk in the streets. They make fires and block roads. Police use tear gas to stop them. President Adama Barrow calls the problem a big emergency. He says that the government will bring a new power machine by the end of October 2026.

Officials say that hot weather causes the troubles. This is a big problem because the country has an election in December.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Gambian President Adama Barrow promised to fix the country’s big electricity problems by the end of October 2026. This happened after angry people protested in the streets.

Demonstrators in the capital burned tires and blocked traffic because some areas had no power for two days during very hot weather. Police used tear gas to stop the crowd near the power company building. People are upset because food spoils and businesses cannot work without electricity.

President Barrow called the blackouts a serious emergency. He said the government will finish building a new power machine soon to help homes and businesses. Energy leaders said hot weather and foreign problems caused the power shortages. These protests are important because the country will hold elections in December, and Barrow wants to win again.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Gambian President Adama Barrow promised to improve the country’s severe power outages by the end of October. His announcement followed intense overnight protests in the capital, Banjul, and surrounding areas.

Demonstrators blocked roads, set fires, and marched toward the headquarters of the national energy provider, NAWEC. Police used tear gas to disperse the crowds.

Residents expressed frustration over spoiled food and interrupted businesses after enduring blackouts lasting up to 48 hours during extreme summer heat. President Barrow declared the crisis a national security issue and an emergency. To address the shortage, the government is installing a new 24-megawatt generator and planning a 50-megawatt solar power plant.

NAWEC officials attributed the blackouts to rising demand, climate change, and Middle Eastern conflict impacting imports. These unrests mark a major escalation just months before the December presidential election, where Barrow is seeking a third term.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
A flashbulb memory is a special picture in your mind of a big event, like the September 11 attacks in New York. People remember the moment. They know the place and feeling in that moment. They feel very sure about their memory.

But scientists say that our brains make many mistakes over time. We add new information from the news or friends, so the story changes. Strong feelings make memories feel very clear. Even important leaders, like President Bush, forgets small details about that day.

When we share memories, we feel closer to each other. Today, news changes fast. People may share fewer of these big memories together in the future.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
A flashbulb memory is a strong memory of where you were during a big world event, like the September 11 attacks. People feel very sure about these memories, but scientists say they can be wrong.

Every time we remember something, our brain changes the details. Studies show that people change about 40 percent of the details after one year. Big emotions change how the brain saves memories. Strong feelings make us remember events clearly, but we still make mistakes. For example, President George W. Bush misremembered how he first heard about the 9/11 plane crash.

Flashbulb memories help us feel connected to other people because we shared the same big experience. Today, because news comes from many different sources, fewer large groups will share the exact same flashbulb memories in the future.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
A flashbulb memory is a vivid recollection of learning about a major, highly emotional public event, such as the September 11 terror attacks. Although people feel absolute confidence in these memories, research shows they are not entirely accurate.

Memories are dynamic; each time a person retrieves one, the hippocampus updates it with new information from media or conversations. In fact, studies reveal that people alter roughly 40 percent of their personal details within a year. Unlike regular memories, emotional events activate the amygdala, which focuses attention and embeds the experience more strongly. These memories also strengthen social connection, because they create a shared sense of identity among groups.

Even prominent figures, including President George W. Bush, have famously mixed up the timeline of how they learned about the 9/11 attacks due to repeated exposure to news footage. Because modern media is highly fragmented, widespread flashbulb memories shared by whole nations may become less common in the future.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Pop Mart is a toy company from China. Its toy Labubu is very popular in many countries.

The company wants Labubu to be successful for a long time, like Disney’s Mickey Mouse. Pop Mart also wants to make more toys like Labubu. Now, Pop Mart is bigger than many other toy companies.

Because of Labubu, many new companies in China also want to make toys. More people want to buy and sell art toys. Pop Mart sells toys in ‘blind boxes,’ so people do not know which toy they get. This makes it more fun and special.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Pop Mart is a Chinese company that makes art toys. Its most famous toy is Labubu, which is popular all around the world.

The company is learning from Disney and wants Labubu to stay successful for many years, not just now. Pop Mart also wants to create other toys with the same level of success. It is already bigger in value than famous toy companies like Hasbro and Mattel.

The success of Labubu brought more competition to the art toy market in China. Many new companies and artists want to join this business. Pop Mart uses the ‘blind box’ system, where buyers don’t know which toy they will get, and it attracts many young women.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Pop Mart, a Chinese toy company, has achieved global success with its character Labubu.

The company’s strategy is inspired by Disney, aiming to turn short-term popularity into long-term growth. Like Disney’s Mickey Mouse, Labubu is becoming a strong intellectual property with potential for theme parks, entertainment, and merchandise. Pop Mart doesn’t want only one big hit. Instead, it hopes to create five to ten characters with similar global potential. The company is now more valuable than major toy makers like Hasbro, Mattel, and Sanrio.

Labubu’s success has also increased competition in China’s art toy industry, where many new companies and artists are trying to enter the market. Pop Mart’s ‘blind box’ model and focus on young women helped its growth, but critics say it still depends too much on Labubu. Analysts note the firm faces challenges if it wants to repeat Disney’s success, but its fast rise shows strong foundations.

title: World News for Students of English

1.title: World News for Students of English
1.content:
Swedish scientists do an experiment. They put a cloth on a glacier. The glacier is the Helags Glacier in the north of Sweden.

All glaciers in the world are melting. This happens because the planet is getting warmer. Scientists are thinking of ways on how to stop it.

They put a cloth on the top of the Helags Glacier in summer. The cloth stops the sun. It keeps the glacier cold. Scientists save at least 3.5 meters of ice. The ice does not melt.

The melting of glaciers is a serious problem. Scientists believe that more people know about the problem now.

2.title: World News for Students of English
2.content:
Swedish scientists did an experiment on the Helags Glacier in the north of the country.

The scientists put a special cloth on the top of the glacier during the summer months. The cloth was made of very strong and durable material which blocked the sun and UV radiation. It also kept the glacier cold.

The team said that they saved at least 3.5 meters of ice from melting. Glaciers are melting all over the world as a result of warmer temperatures. It is important that more people know about the problem because it will be more serious in the future, and people will have to solve it.

3.title: World News for Students of English
3.content:
Researchers performed an experiment on the Helags Glacier in northern Sweden.

They used a cloth sheet to shield a part of the glacier over the summer, and they said that the cloth saved at least 3.5 meters in height from melting. The sheet was about one and a half meters thick, and it was very strong and durable. It hindered the sun and UV radiation, and it also isolated the ice from warm air.

Global warming is causing glaciers to shrink all over the world, and researchers hope to redo their test on a larger size, so they can raise awareness about the dangers many people will face if the glaciers disappear.
